contexts.text: With the struggles of God I have struggled with my sister, and I have prevailed () = in the supreme sense, the Divine power; in the internal, temptation in which he overcomes; in the external, resistance by the natural man. For the struggles of God, and to struggle = temptations; for temptations are nothing else than the struggles of the internal man with the external. Explained.
Naphtali was named from struggles (which = temptations. AC 6412).
The wrestlings of temptations. Treated of.
Finally, Jacob wrestled with an Angel, by which wrestling is signified temptation, AC 4273. (See Stubborn, at AE 710:20.)
There wrestled a man with him () = temptation as to truth; for to wrestle = temptation. Temptation itself is nothing else than a wrestling, or combat. Explained.
Let me go, that is, from wrestling with me, = that the temptation ceased.
That the wrestling was begun before the dawn arose, and ceased after it arose... = states of conjunction through temptations. Explained.
Temptations and victories in them are what make man spiritual; for which reason Jacob was first named Israel after he had wrestled.
That not good, but evil Spirits, are signified by him who wrestled with Jacob, may be evident from the fact that by wrestling is signified temptation. Explained.
Hence it is that he who wrestled with Jacob was not willing to reveal his name.
That in the internal spiritual sense by him who wrestled with Jacob is meant the angelic Heaven, is because the Lord... admitted even the Angels to tempt Him...
Unless he performs serious repentance, and for a long time afterwards struggles with falsities and evils.
Man cannot (remove these evils) except... with a struggle, thus with combat.
If he enters their Heaven his life struggles with death.
This pure love... perpetually struggles with those in Hell, and fights for them against the devil...
In those things which are contrary to order... God is omnipresent by a continual struggle with them...
On the wrestling of God with Jacob. General article.
The struggles of God = spiritual temptations.
